title: Sushant Singh Rajput's Sister Shweta Reveals Actor Was Deeply Disturbed After Disha Salian's Death
excerpt: In a podcast interview, Shweta Singh Kirti questioned the official suicide finding, pointing to physical inconsistencies at the scene and revealing her brother's distress in his final days.
body:
• Shweta Singh Kirti said Sushant was deeply troubled after former manager Disha Salian's death on June 8, 2020, just days before his own passing on June 14
  • She questioned the suicide finding, citing insufficient space between the bed and fan, missing room keys, and a locked door Sushant never locked
  • The CBI concluded Salian's death was accidental but confirmed Sushant had searched news reports linking him to Salian in the week before his death
  • Shweta, who is based in the United States, has renewed her plea for a thorough CBI investigation into her brother's case

Shweta Questions the Official Account

Sushant Singh Rajput's elder sister Shweta Singh Kirti has once again raised pointed questions about the circumstances surrounding the Bollywood actor's death, revealing that he was visibly disturbed after former manager Disha Salian died on June 8, 2020 — just six days before he was found dead at his Mumbai apartment.

https://x.com/DeccanHerald/status/2087842259655901596

In a podcast interview with Shubhankar Mishra, Shweta challenged the official suicide ruling, zeroing in on what she described as physical impossibilities at the scene.

"How can it be suicide? The fan and the bed didn't have enough distance between them for a person to hang there. There was no distance at all."

— Shweta Singh Kirti, podcast interview

Shweta pointed out that no stool or elevated surface was found in the room — an essential element if someone were to reach the ceiling fan. She also noted that the marks on Sushant's neck did not resemble those left by a dupatta or cloth, describing them instead as marks from "something like a thin chain."

Missing Keys and Locked Doors

In a separate interview with Ranveer Allahabadia, Shweta expanded on the inconsistencies she has flagged. She said the keys to Sushant's room were missing, according to the building's management, and that his door was locked — something the actor never did, according to Bollywood Hungama.

"All nearby CCTVs were also not working that day. There are a lot of things which do not make sense," Shweta said during the interview. She also revealed that the family was not allowed to enter Sushant's flat after his death, limiting their ability to examine the scene independently.

The Disha Salian Connection

Disha Salian, a 28-year-old celebrity manager who had briefly worked with Sushant, fell from the 14th floor of her Mumbai apartment on the night of June 8-9, 2020. The CBI later concluded her death was accidental — she had consumed alcohol at a birthday gathering and lost her balance, according to The Economic Times.

A CBI official stated that "other than a few chats, which were in connection to a brand-building exercise, nothing more was found between Salian and Rajput." However, the official confirmed that Sushant had searched Google for news reports linking his name to Salian's in the week before his death, according to Bollywood Hungama.

Earlier reports from Times Now revealed that Sushant had contacted a lawyer after Salian's death — the same day his girlfriend Rhea Chakraborty moved out of his home. He also reportedly deleted his hard disks with the help of flatmate Siddharth Pithani after finding articles connecting him to Salian, according to Bollywood Life.

Family's Ongoing Fight for Justice

Despite the CBI declaring that the two deaths were unrelated, Sushant's family has challenged the investigation's closure report. Shweta, who is based in the United States, has been the most vocal family member, previously launching social media campaigns including #UnitedForSSRJustice and calling for a "people's movement" to press for a thorough investigation.

"I am not an investigator, I cannot investigate the case," Shweta told Allahabadia. "I want CBI to tell us what happened. Whatever happened, give us proof and let us know."

Sushant's death in June 2020 triggered one of the most intense public and media investigations in Indian entertainment history, with allegations swirling around nepotism, industry practices, and the role of those close to the actor. His girlfriend Rhea Chakraborty was later given a clean chit in the case.

Why the Diaspora Still Cares

The case has remained particularly resonant among the Indian diaspora community, with NRIs in the United States, United Kingdom, and Middle East organizing vigils, billboard campaigns, and social media drives demanding justice. Shweta's own presence in the US has kept the diaspora closely connected to the family's ongoing efforts. Nearly six years after his death, the case continues to surface periodically as family members raise new questions and push back against the official findings.
nri_angle: Sushant Singh Rajput's death triggered massive diaspora mobilization, with NRIs organizing vigils and billboard campaigns; his US-based sister Shweta has kept the community engaged in the fight for justice.
